items.question: Which animals may serve as the sacrificial offering in this rite?
premises: A jackal is listed as an offering
A deer or buffalo is listed as an offering
A rhinoceros is likewise listed as an offering
items.inference: Multiple kinds of animals are permitted as sacrificial offerings.
uncertainties: The exact ritual role of these animals depends on the surrounding context.
items.plain_english: A jackal, a deer, or also a buffalo, and likewise a rhinoceros.

items.question: What qualities and karmic limit characterize the sacrificial animal?
premises: The animal possesses knowledge, strength, and capability
Its condition extends to the end of seven births
These attributes define the animal in this context
items.inference: The sacrificial animal is endowed with notable powers affecting seven births.
uncertainties: The precise sense of knowledge in an animal is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: The animal has knowledge, strength, and capability extending to the end of seven births.

items.question: How should the multitude of yoginis be honored in this ritual?
premises: The yogini multitude is the object of worship
Offerings include food, eatables, and other items
The instruction is addressed to the beloved
items.inference: One should worship the multitude of yoginis with food, eatables, and similar offerings.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should worship the multitude of yoginis with food, eatables, and other offerings.

items.question: In what three flavor forms should the ritual meat be prepared?
premises: Meat is to be prepared as an offering
It should be made in three varieties
The varieties are alkaline, sour, and sweet
items.inference: The ritual meat must be prepared in alkaline, sour, and sweet forms.
uncertainties: The exact meaning of pakṣa as a flavor category is uncertain.
items.plain_english: One should prepare the meat in three ways: alkaline, sour, and likewise sweet.

items.question: What plant-derived substances are permitted as alternative offerings?
premises: Substances born from trees are included
Substances born from roots are included
Substances born from flowers or fruits are also included
items.inference: Offerings may be derived from trees, roots, flowers, or fruits.
uncertainties: The syntactic connection to the previous verse's injunction is implied.
items.plain_english: Those born from trees, born from roots, and indeed born from flowers, or also born from fruits.

items.question: How must the practice of non-duality be carried out according to the teaching?
premises: Non-duality has been declared in a specific way
It must be performed as declared
It must not be performed otherwise
items.inference: The practice of non-duality must follow the teaching exactly and not deviate.
items.plain_english: Non-duality must be practiced just as it has been declared, and never otherwise.

items.question: What consequence befalls those who violate the prescribed non-dual practice?
premises: Transgressors fall into hell
The hells named include terrible, Avici, and Raurava
This is stated as a certain consequence
items.inference: Violators of the teaching fall into terrible hells such as Avici and Raurava.
items.plain_english: They fall into terrible hell, into Avici and likewise into Raurava.

items.question: Who is designated as the sacrificial animal within the Kula tradition?
premises: The subject is situated in the midst of the yogini group
He is identified as the animal
This designation is proclaimed in the Kula
items.inference: In the Kula, the one placed in the midst of the yogini group is called the animal.
uncertainties: Whether paśu is literal or symbolic is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: In the Kula, he who is situated in the midst of the group of yoginis is called the animal.

items.question: With what protective attitude should one guard the designated person?
premises: A comparison is made to a mother protecting a child
The child is born from the mother's lover
The protection is to be given as to one's own son
items.inference: One should protect that person just as a mother protects her own son born of a lover.
uncertainties: The metaphorical application to the ritual context is implied.
items.plain_english: One should protect him just as a mother protects her own son born from her lover.

items.question: What supernatural accomplishments may arise as a result of this practice?
premises: The siddhis include minuteness and other powers
These are qualities of lordship
A mental accomplishment may also arise
items.inference: The practice may yield the siddhis such as minuteness and other lordly powers, including mental accomplishment.
items.plain_english: The accomplishment of lordship, such as minuteness and other powers, and mental accomplishment may arise.

items.question: What must be understood as bondage and what must be understood as liberation?
premises: Bondage is characterized by ignorance
Knowledge is to be known as liberation
Both bondage and liberation are objects of understanding
items.inference: Ignorance is to be known as bondage, and knowledge is to be known as liberation.
items.plain_english: Bondage through ignorance is to be known; knowledge is to be known as liberation.

items.question: How does the realized yogin remain unaffected by actions and their results?
premises: Water rests on a lotus leaf without clinging
This image illustrates non-attachment
The yogin is likewise not tainted
items.inference: Just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, the yogin is not tainted.
items.plain_english: Just as water on a lotus leaf, so too one is not tainted.

items.question: What range of karmic results, both sinful and meritorious, is considered here?
premises: Sins such as killing a brahmin are included
Merits such as the horse sacrifice are included
Both extremes of karmic fruit are named
items.inference: Both grave sins and great merits are encompassed in this consideration.
items.plain_english: Sin such as the killing of a brahmin, and merit such as the horse sacrifice and others.

items.question: Why do karmic merits and sins fail to bind the accomplished yogin?
premises: The yogin is not seized by these karmic results
This holds even when such acts are being performed
The statement is made clearly
items.inference: The yogin remains unbound by karmic merits and sins, even while acts are performed.
items.plain_english: The yogin is clearly not seized by these, even when they are being performed.

items.question: What mistaken practices should not be imposed in this non-dual discipline?
premises: Non-possession and contentment are named
Union of dualities is named
One should not enforce these as external practices
items.inference: One should not artificially impose non-possession, contentment, or dualistic union.
uncertainties: The exact target of the prohibition is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: One should not enforce mere non-possession, contentment, or the union of dualities.

items.question: What attitude must be maintained toward the sacred offering and the vow of non-duality?
premises: The sacred offering must not be reviled
The vow is characterized by non-duality
The instruction is addressed to the fair one
items.inference: One must not revile the sacred offering, for the vow is indeed non-duality.
items.plain_english: O fair one, one should not revile the sacred offering, for the vow is indeed non-duality.

items.question: To whom is this sacred offering always especially dear?
premises: The offering is dear to siddhas
The offering is dear to yoginis
This preference holds always
items.inference: This sacred offering is always dear to the siddhas and yoginis.
items.plain_english: This sacred offering is always dear to the siddhas and the yoginis.

items.question: Which ritual substances are enumerated for use in this offering?
premises: The vuka flower and Shiva's water are listed
Blood and semen are listed
Liquor is likewise listed
items.inference: The offering includes vuka flower, Shiva's water, blood, semen, and liquor.
uncertainties: The exact identity of vuka and śiva-ambu is tradition-specific.
items.plain_english: The vuka flower, Shiva's water, blood and semen, and likewise liquor.

items.question: What additional offerings accompany the ritual substances previously listed?
premises: Fragrance and incense are included
Song and betel are included
A red garment is included
items.inference: The ritual also includes fragrance, incense, song, betel, and a red garment.
items.plain_english: Fragrance, incense, song, betel, and a red garment.

items.question: Through what means does the unfolding of true knowledge occur?
premises: The unfolding of knowledge arises in this way
It does not arise through other service
The statement is addressed to the fair one
items.inference: True knowledge unfolds through this practice and not through other forms of service.
items.plain_english: O fair one, the unfolding of knowledge occurs in this way, and not through any other service.

items.question: What characterizes a person who merely mocks the Kula scripture?
premises: Such a person is driven by greed
Such a person is always fickle
This behavior amounts to mockery of the Kula scripture
items.inference: One who seeks out of greed and is always fickle makes a mockery of the Kula scripture.
uncertainties: The grammatical agreement of capalā with the subject is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: One who seeks out of greed and is always fickle is a mockery of the Kula scripture.

items.question: Within what period can one become a recipient of accomplishment through Kula knowledge?
premises: Accomplishment arises from the enjoyment of Kula knowledge
A period of six months is specified
One becomes a fit recipient of siddhi
items.inference: Through the enjoyment of Kula knowledge, one becomes a recipient of accomplishment within six months.
items.plain_english: Through the enjoyment of Kula knowledge, one becomes a recipient of accomplishment in six months.

items.question: When should the ritual substance be consumed in relation to the yogini assembly?
premises: That substance should be consumed
It should be done always at the proper time
The yogini assembly should take place
items.inference: One should always consume that substance at the time when the yogini assembly occurs.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation between drinking and the assembly is compressed.
items.plain_english: One should always drink that at the proper time when there is an assembly of yoginis.

items.question: What is the higher significance of the constant washing of the mouth?
premises: Washing of the mouth is performed always
It is related to Brahman
It is described as having gone upward
items.inference: The constant washing of the mouth is understood as an upward movement toward Brahman.
uncertainties: The ritual and symbolic meaning of ūrddha gatam is open to interpretation.
items.plain_english: O beloved, the constant washing of the mouth is the upward movement toward Brahman.
